'''Antonio V. Arizabal Jr.''' (born October 13, 1932) is a Filipino chemist who served as Secretary of the [[Department of Science and Technology (Philippines)|Department of Science and Technology]] of the [[Philippines]].

==Early life and education==
Antonio V. Arizabal Jr.<ref>{{cite web |title=16 years of M&E Week |url=https://metalsweek.dost.gov.ph/2024/about-metals-and-engineering-week.html |website=M&E Week Blog |publisher=Department of Science and Technology |access-date=1 March 2026}}</ref> was born on October 13, 1932, in [[Manila]]. He obtained a bachelor's degree in [[chemistry]] from the [[University of the Philippines]] and a masters and doctorate in [[metallurgy]] from the [[Carnegie Mellon University|Carnegie Institute of Technology]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web |last1=Celestial |first1=Dunn Alfredo A. |title=The DOST Secretary |url=https://www.dost.gov.ph/transparency/about-dost/the-secretary.html#1986-1989-dr-antonio-v-arizabal |website=www.dost.gov.ph |language=en-gb |date=1 August 2014}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1971, he was executive director of the Metals Industry Research and Development Center and an ex-officio trustee of the Philippine Iron and Steel Institute.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Our History |url=http://philippineironsteel.org/our-history |access-date=2026-03-01 |website=philippineironsteel.org}}</ref> Arizabal was a former CEO for [[Iligan Steel Mill|National Steel Corp]] and served as a receiver in 2000.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Felix |first=Rocel |title=SEC names interim receiver for NSC |url=https://www.philstar.com/business/2000/03/03/100946/sec-names-interim-receiver-nsc |access-date=2026-03-01 |website=Philstar.com}}</ref>

Arizabal held the top National Science and Technology Authority position and transitioned to the inaugural [[Secretary of Science and Technology (Philippines)|Secretary of Science and Technology]],<ref name=":0" /> holding the position from January 30, 1987, to April 6, 1989.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Parnala |first=Adam |date=2022-08-21 |title=LIST: All the DOST Secretaries in the Philippines |url=https://www.noypigeeks.com/government/dost-secretaries/ |access-date=2026-03-01 |website=NoypiGeeks |language=en-US}}</ref> During his tenure, the Food and Nutrition Research Institute's supplemental food formulations helped feed 80,000 malnourished children in Negros Occidental.<ref name=":0" />
